measures.name: Amendment 3
measures.title: Repeal 2024 abortion-rights amendment
measures.summary: Repeals the 2024 abortion-rights amendment so abortion is allowed only for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, and rape or incest before 12 weeks, requires parental consent for minors, and bans gender-transition procedures for minors.

measures.name: Proposition A
measures.title: Congressional map veto referendum
measures.summary: Approves the legislature's 2025 mid-decade congressional map (HB 1, 2025 Second Extraordinary Session), which dismantles the Democratic-leaning Kansas City 5th District; a No vote keeps the 2022 map.

measures.name: Question 6
measures.title: Right to abortion (second vote)
measures.summary: Gives final approval to a state constitutional right to abortion up to fetal viability, and afterward when needed to protect the pregnant patient's life or health.

measures.name: Question 1
measures.title: Right to reproductive freedom
measures.summary: Adds a fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including abortion, to the Virginia Constitution, allowing third-trimester abortion limits except when the patient's life or health is at risk or the fetus is not viable.

measures.name: Question 2
measures.title: Repeal same-sex marriage ban
measures.summary: Removes Virginia's (unenforceable) constitutional ban on same-sex marriage and affirms that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race, with all lawful marriages treated equally.

measures.name: Proposition 1
measures.title: Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act
measures.summary: Enacts a state-law right to abortion before fetal viability (and after viability in medical emergencies) plus rights to contraception, fertility, prenatal and postpartum care, overriding Idaho's near-total abortion ban.

measures.name: Proposition 40
measures.title: One-time billionaire wealth tax
measures.summary: Imposes a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of California-resident billionaires, with revenue mainly for health care and smaller shares for food assistance and education.

measures.name: Proposition 39
measures.title: Voter ID requirement
measures.summary: Amends the state constitution to require government-issued ID to vote in person (last four digits of an ID number on mail ballots) and requires officials to verify voters' citizenship.

measures.name: Question 8
measures.title: End recreational marijuana sales
measures.summary: Repeals the 2016 law allowing licensed retail sale (and home cultivation) of recreational marijuana; medical marijuana and decriminalized possession remain.

measures.name: Question 9
measures.title: Referendum on 2024 gun law
measures.summary: Keeps the 2024 firearms law (assault-style firearm ban, ghost-gun rules, expanded extreme-risk orders, age-21 limits on semiautomatic long guns) in place; a No vote repeals it.

measures.name: Initiative 645
measures.title: Repeal millionaires income tax
measures.summary: Repeals the 9.9% tax on household income over $1 million enacted in March 2026 and prohibits future state and local taxes on income.

measures.name: Measure 2
measures.title: Repeal top-four primary and RCV
measures.summary: Repeals Alaska's nonpartisan top-four primary, ranked-choice general elections, and 2020 campaign-finance disclosure rules, restoring party primaries and single-choice plurality elections.

measures.name: Amendment 3
measures.title: Homestead property tax exemption
measures.summary: Raises the homestead exemption from non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and cuts the annual assessment-increase cap on non-homestead property from 10% to 5%.

measures.name: Amendment 81
measures.title: Notify DHS of charged noncitizens
measures.summary: Requires state and local law enforcement to notify the U.S. Department of Homeland Security within 72 hours when someone charged with a violent crime, or with a prior felony, cannot be confirmed to be lawfully present in the U.S.

measures.name: Question 3
measures.title: Drop congressional map criteria
measures.summary: Removes state constitutional criteria (compactness, contiguity, respect for boundaries) from congressional districts, keeping them for legislative districts, and lets the legislature give the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction over congressional-map challenges.

insights.title: House: Democrats favored (89%)
insights.body: Democrats win 230 seats in the median simulation (80% range 217–244); 218 is a majority. They hold 214 going in.

insights.title: Senate: Democrats slightly favored (64%)
insights.body: Democrats need 51 seats; Republicans need 50, because the Vice President breaks ties. 34 Democratic-caucus and 31 Republican seats are not up. In 1% of simulations neither side reaches its number without an unaligned independent.

insights.title: Most likely outcome: Democrats win both chambers (63%)
insights.body: Divided Congress in 26% of simulations; Democrats win both in 63%, Republicans keep both in 11%.

insights.title: Senate tipping point: Ohio (special)
insights.body: The race that would give Democrats their 51st seat, by share of simulations: Ohio (special) 16%, Texas 15%, Alaska 14%.

insights.title: Biggest swing race: Ohio (special)
insights.body: If the Democrat wins Ohio (special), Democrats control the Senate in 84% of simulations; if the Republican wins, 34%.

insights.title: House seats most likely to decide control
insights.body: The 218th Democratic seat is most often: CA-22 (3%), IA-3 (3%), FL-25 (3%), PA-8 (3%), IA-1 (3%).

insights.title: 13 Senate/governor seats with a 30%+ chance to flip
insights.body: North Carolina Senate (R-held, 98%); Alaska Governor (R-held, 96%); Iowa Governor (R-held, 92%); Ohio Governor (R-held, 83%); Maine Senate (R-held, 75%); Kansas Governor (D-held, 74%).

insights.title: 145 districts are on new maps
insights.body: Across the redrawn districts Democrats are expected to win 69.8 seats (incumbents running there: 66 Democrats). New lines mean less history to lean on, so these seats carry wider uncertainty.

insights.title: National environment: D+7.9
insights.body: Generic-ballot average +8.0 (70 polls, weight 75%), midterm fundamentals +7.5. Democrats win the national House vote in 99% of simulations.

insights.title: Governors: Democrats expected to hold 27.3 of 50
insights.body: 36 races this year; Democrats hold a majority of governorships in 83% of simulations.
